instructions.purpose: Dry-run a scheduled job that uses automations and show the exact message it would send if it fired now. Use this tool before attaching automations to a job, changing its automations list, or creating a job with automations, so the user can see the result and confirm before anything is saved.

tool.name: preview-cron-job
tool.description: Runs the job's automations in order with real data, then builds the message the same way a real firing does: with a taskPrompt the scheduled-task agent writes it from the automation outputs; without a taskPrompt the automations' text outputs are joined as written. Nothing is delivered, nothing is saved to history, and automation state and failure counts are not changed. Returns message (absent when nothing would be sent), note explaining an empty result, and automations with each automation's outcome and error.

usage_rules.rule: Call this before schedule-once, schedule-recurring, or update-cron-job whenever the job will run a new or changed automations list; removing every automation from a job needs no preview
For an existing job pass its name and only the values that would change; taskPrompt and automations override the job's current values, and automations replaces the whole list
For a job that does not exist yet omit name and pass the planned taskPrompt (if any) and automations
Pass automations as saved automation names in the order they should run
Return the previewed message and any failed or unavailable automations so Main can show them to the user, and say the change is not saved yet
Save the change only after the user confirms the preview; any clear agreement counts as confirmation
If an automation failed or is unavailable, report its error instead of saving; save anyway only when the delegated task says the user accepted that failure

example.context: Delegated task: "Add the weather automation to the morning-briefing job"
example.reasoning: Show the user how the briefing would look with the weather automation before updating the job.

example.context: Delegated task: "Every day at 7 send me the bus-departures automation output"
example.reasoning: A new job without a taskPrompt sends the automation's text as written; preview it before scheduling.
